---
title: "Simple linear regression in `R`"
output: html_document
author: BAM & BIEBAM
---

All code is base `R`. Every number quoted on the Session 28 slides can be reproduced here.
Data: `LifeCycleSavings` (50 countries): `sr` = savings rate (%), `pop15` = % of population under 15.

## Fit and least squares by hand

```{r}
d <- LifeCycleSavings
x <- d$pop15; y <- d$sr; n <- nrow(d)
Sxx <- sum((x - mean(x))^2); Sxy <- sum((x - mean(x)) * (y - mean(y)))
b1 <- Sxy / Sxx; b0 <- mean(y) - b1 * mean(x)
c(b0 = b0, b1 = b1, Sxx = Sxx)                       # 17.4966, -0.2230, 4103.95
cor(x, y) * sd(y) / sd(x)                            # b1 = r * sy / sx
fit <- lm(sr ~ pop15, data = d)
summary(fit)
```

## Residuals, s, sums of squares, R-squared

```{r}
e <- resid(fit)
c(sum_e = sum(e), sum_xe = sum(x * e))               # both 0
SSE <- sum(e^2); SST <- sum((y - mean(y))^2); SSR <- SST - SSE
c(SSE = SSE, SST = SST, SSR = SSR, s2 = SSE / (n - 2), s = sqrt(SSE / (n - 2)))
c(R2 = SSR / SST, r2 = cor(x, y)^2, r = cor(x, y))   # 0.2075, 0.2075, -0.4555
anova(fit)                                           # F = 12.57, p = 0.00089
```

## Inference on the slope

```{r}
se <- sqrt(SSE / (n - 2) / Sxx)
c(se = se, t = b1 / se, p = 2 * pt(-abs(b1 / se), n - 2), t_crit = qt(0.975, n - 2))
b1 + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, n - 2) * se                # (-0.349, -0.097)
confint(fit)
(b1 / se)^2                                          # F = t^2 = 12.57
```

## Confidence and prediction intervals at pop15 = 30

```{r}
new <- data.frame(pop15 = 30)
predict(fit, new)                                    # 10.81
predict(fit, new, interval = "confidence")           # (9.49, 12.12)
predict(fit, new, interval = "prediction")           # (2.60, 19.01)
h <- 1 / n + (30 - mean(x))^2 / Sxx
sqrt(SSE / (n - 2)) * sqrt(c(CI = h, PI = 1 + h))    # standard errors
```

## Matrix form and hat matrix

```{r}
X <- cbind(1, x)
beta <- solve(t(X) %*% X, t(X) %*% y); drop(beta)
H <- X %*% solve(t(X) %*% X) %*% t(X)
c(trace = sum(diag(H)), max_leverage = max(diag(H)))  # 2, 0.065
all.equal(drop(H %*% y), unname(fitted(fit)))
```

## Your turn answers (other data)

```{r}
r <- 0.8; sx <- 2; sy <- 6
b1 <- r * sy / sx; b0 <- 50 - b1 * 10; c(b1, b0, b0 + b1 * 12)   # 2.4, 26, 54.8
c(r = -sqrt(0.49), unexplained = 1 - 0.49, SSR = 0.49 * 200, SSE = 0.51 * 200)
fit2 <- lm(sr ~ ddpi, data = d); summary(fit2); confint(fit2)
predict(fit2, data.frame(ddpi = 3))                  # 9.31
3.2 / 1.0                                            # exit ticket: t = 3.2 > 2.086
```

## Diagnostics

```{r}
sort(abs(rstandard(fit)), decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]    # Zambia 2.83, Japan 2.43, Iceland 2.17
sort(hatvalues(fit), decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]
2 * 2 / n                                            # rule of thumb 2p/n = 0.08
par(mfrow = c(2, 2)); plot(fit)
```

## Simulation: sampling distribution of the slope

```{r}
set.seed(28)
b <- coef(fit); s <- summary(fit)$sigma
sl <- replicate(3000, coef(lm(b[1] + b[2] * x + rnorm(n, 0, s) ~ x))[2])
c(mean = mean(sl), sd = sd(sl), theory_sd = s / sqrt(Sxx))   # -0.224, 0.063, 0.0629
```

## Anscombe's quartet

```{r}
sapply(1:4, function(i) c(r = cor(anscombe[[i]], anscombe[[i + 4]]),
                          coef(lm(anscombe[[i + 4]] ~ anscombe[[i]]))))
```
